newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR LARGELY STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR LARGELY STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted steady against most currencies in lacklustre Tuesday morning trade.
But foreign exchange dealers expected it to start appreciating in coming weeks on the back of inflows from the annual tobacco sales opening on Tuesday and running until October.
"But at the moment it's very stable. People are cautiously watching the tobacco sales," said one dealer.

At around 0800 GMT, the local unit was trading at 11.2850/2950 against the U.S. dollar, where it closed Monday's session, was also unchanged versus the mark at 6.6300/6500 and at 2.5400/5500 against South Africa's rand.
It however weakened on sterling to 18.4800/5000 from 18.4500/4700.
